nota: Personaje con caida (los dos mejores personajes medidos: ronald-wayne 0.84, jesse-livermore 0.82, ambos historias de perdida). Enlaza con la senal del dia ('stock sinks', todos en la misma accion). Fuente primaria leida: Odlyzko, Physics Today jul-2020 (DOI 10.1063/PT.3.4521). La frase 'madness of people' es 'allegedly': no se usa como cita.

frases.texto: You would never buy a stock at the top. Isaac Newton did.
He ran the Royal Mint.
In April seventeen twenty, he decided the South Sea boom would end badly, and sold.
His profit was about twenty thousand pounds.
But the stock kept climbing without him.
By June, he put nearly everything back in, almost at the peak.
By October, the stock was worth under a quarter of that peak.
He lost the whole profit, and a good bit more.
He was still rich. Only with a third less than before the bubble.
Even Newton bought at the top. Seeing the bubble was the easy part.
Your instincts say sell before the crash. Isaac Newton did exactly that, and still lost.
He ran the Royal Mint.
That April, he sold his South Sea shares for a profit of about twenty thousand pounds.
So how did he lose?
The stock kept climbing without him.
By June, he put nearly everything back in, almost at the peak.
By October, the stock was worth under a quarter of that peak.
The profit was gone, and a good bit more.
He was still rich. Only with a third less than before the bubble.
He sold before the crash. Staying out was the part he couldn't do.
